description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2024: Experimental Investigation on Tsunami-Driven Debris Damming at Elevated Coastal Structures is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Sabarethinam Kameshwar, Louisiana State University (lsu.edu). This experimental project investigated the mechanisms leading to debris accumulation in front of structures during tsunamis (debris damming) and induced loadings on the columns of the structures due to debris damming. The study was conducted through the construction of a 1:20 geometric scale physical model. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-na8y-c575. Keywords: Large Wave Flume Oregon State University, Experiment, Tsunami, Debris Damming, Coastal Structure. Published 2024-07-17. Facility named: Large Wave Flume and Directional Wave Basin - Oregon State University. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
